issues.where: where the cliff and lava fan meet the foreground floor, about y 88% across the full width
issues.what: the land stops on a dead-straight horizontal edge, with a thin glowing line along it, and below it is a flat, featureless dark plane. It reads as a seam between two separate sets, not as ground running into the cliff. The lava fan stops on that line with no pool, crust or spread onto the floor
issues.fix: carry the rubble slope and lava apron down into the floor, break up the edge, and give the lava a toe that spreads, crusts and lights the floor in front of it

issues.where: the base of the far cliff, about y 55%, from x 0 to 45%
issues.what: the same dead-straight glowing horizon line. The lava falls end on a ruler-flat seam and the floor in front is an untextured plane with no air or detail running back to the cliff
issues.fix: build a real talus and toe at the cliff base, let the ground rise into it, and break the line with fume and rubble

issues.where: the fog behind the right-hand creature's neck, x 83 to 100%, y 0 to 45%, shown in the crop at x 83 to 100%, y 25 to 42%
issues.what: thin vertical dotted lines run straight down through the haze. They look like seams between render tiles or the edges of fog cards, and they are visible at native size
issues.fix: remove the card or tile seams, either with one continuous volume or by re-rendering without tile boundaries

issues.where: the cave mouth and the lip below it, x 27 to 60%, y 8 to 35%
issues.what: the cave opening is a flat, uniform brown blob with no interior depth, rock or falloff, like a hole cut in a backdrop. The lit rock under the lip has smeared, swirled texture stretched like clay
issues.fix: give the cave an interior: back wall, ceiling falloff, and glow from the lava source lighting the inside. Re-project the lip texture so it isn't smeared

issues.where: the lava fan and cascade, x 38 to 72%, y 45 to 88%
issues.what: the lava reads as glossy, stretched streaks on a plastic or clay surface. It has orange contour stripes but no crust plates, no dark cooled skin and no incandescent cracks. The glow sits on the surface and barely lights the rock beside it or the fume above
issues.fix: add a cooled crust broken by bright seams, give the falls thickness and spatter, and let the lava bounce-light the nearby rock and the haze

issues.where: the lava ribbons across the foreground floor
issues.what: the rivers are thin, flat painted lines lying on the ground. They have no channel, levee, crust edge or heat shimmer, and they cast no glow on the ground or on the creature's feet and the root-like foot that crosses them
issues.fix: cut the flows into a channel with a crusted rim, and add local glow on the surrounding ground and on any limb nearby

issues.what: every foot ends in an identical smooth grey disc, like a plastic puck or a base plate. The discs look placed on the floor rather than pressing into it, with no contact shadow, displacement or ash on them
issues.fix: vary the feet, sink them into the ground with a contact shadow and displaced or crusted ground, and dust them with ash

issues.where: the foreground floor, x 0 to 58%, y 58 to 75%
issues.what: the ground texture smears into horizontal streaks, as if stretched along one axis. The whole floor is a single uniform material with no rocks, cracks or ash variation
issues.fix: fix the UV or projection stretch, and add scattered clinker, cracks and variation in material

issues.where: the cliff face on the left, x 0 to 30%
issues.what: faint vertical banding and repeated horizontal strata give a tiled look
issues.fix: break up the repetition with larger-scale variation

issues.where: the glowing plume on the right, x 65 to 90%, y 35 to 85%
issues.what: the plume glows orange at its base with no visible source, and it lights neither the floor nor the cliff beside it
issues.fix: tie the glow to a visible vent or lava, and let it light the ground beneath

issues.where: the two distant creatures, around x 60 to 68%
issues.what: they are near-identical in silhouette and pose

note: After the JSON the critic added: No eyes, ears, text, people or logos were found. The haze gives the far distance some air, which is the strongest element.
